title: Dual-Stopband Quarter-Wave Stack with Thickness Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high-low index stack with 36 layers, where thicknesses are optimized around quarter-wave conditions for both 355nm and 1030nm center wavelengths, will produce two distinct stopbands while maintaining a visible passband between them.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics: quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) creates constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength. High-low index contrast (Ta2O5 ~2.1, SiO2 ~1.46) determines stopband width and depth. Two different quarter-wave periods can coexist in one stack to create dual stopbands.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
soft_objectives: minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm band
minimize average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm band
maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm band
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength when optical thickness equals lambda/4
Index contrast between high-index and low-index materials determines stopband width and peak reflectance
Multiple quarter-wave periods in one stack can create multiple stopbands at different wavelengths
More layer pairs increase stopband depth but also increase passband ripple
expected_advantages: Fixed material order isolates thickness as the only optimization variable
36 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-stopband design
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard deposition processes
known_risks: Ta2O5 name may not resolve in local registry - if rejected, need to use the exact measurement name the registry provides; I recall it as tantalum pentoxide but the exact stoichiometry string matters
Refractive index values are recalled approximations (Ta2O5 ~2.1-2.2, SiO2 ~1.45-1.46 at visible) - actual dispersion at 355nm and 1030nm may differ significantly

Quarter-wave condition at two widely separated wavelengths (355nm vs 1030nm, ratio ~3:1) may create conflicting thickness requirements that cannot be simultaneously satisfied with a single alternating sequence
Passband ripple in 420-700nm may be higher than desired due to stopband interactions
execution_request_english: Optimize a 36-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees, unpolarized light. Stack structure: alternating Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Gao) layers, starting with Ta2O5 (Gao), ending with SiO2 (Gao) before substrate (18 pairs total). All 36 layer thicknesses are optimization variables, each bounded between 20 nm and 350 nm. Target: minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm band, minimize average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm band, maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm band. Use coherent transfer matrix method for spectral calculation.
